subject.title: Feature: guarantee last N raw messages in agent context (survive compaction and session reset)

question: Should OpenClaw add a core session-level last-N raw-message continuity contract, and if so what auth, channel/thread, and clean-reset boundaries must it obey?
rationale: Current code has only narrow opt-in CLI reseed and compaction-local recent-turn preservation; making raw transcript replay a user-facing guarantee changes config defaults, security boundaries, reset semantics, and context-engine contracts.

options.title: Design a bounded core contract
options.body: Specify minTail/carry-forward semantics with explicit auth, channel/thread, manual clean reset, context-window cap, and context-engine/runtime requirements before implementation.

options.title: Keep narrow runtime-specific fixes
options.body: Leave this issue open only as a tracking umbrella while solving individual CLI, Codex, memory, and compaction bugs through narrower issues.

options.title: Decline universal raw replay
options.body: Keep raw transcript replay opt-in and recommend summary or memory-based continuity instead of a last-N raw-message guarantee.

recommendation.title: Design a bounded core contract
recommendation.body: Specify minTail/carry-forward semantics with explicit auth, channel/thread, manual clean reset, context-window cap, and context-engine/runtime requirements before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR 79764 discussion contains the clearest current product/security boundary guidance for raw transcript reseed defaults.
